aim.p: We want everyone to be able to use this service, including people who use screen readers, keyboards or larger text. It aims to meet WCAG 2.1 level AA and the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW 3.0).

works.p: Marathi, Hindi and English; text that follows your phone's text size; keyboard use with a visible focus outline and a skip link; colours with enough contrast; and status shown in words, not by colour alone.

limits.p: The service has not yet been formally audited. Photographs of letters cannot be read by screen readers; the details read from them are shown as text.

contact.p: If something does not work for you, please tell the Minister's office using the contact details below.

footer.office: Office of the Forest Minister, Maharashtra
footer.contact: Contact details will be added here by the office.

legal.draft: Draft for the pilot. The final text will be issued by the Office of the Forest Minister.

collect.p: The letter you hand in at the Janata Darbar, photographs of its pages, and the details read from it: your name, mobile number, address and what you are asking for.

why.p: Only to register your application, send it to the department that can act on it, and let you check its status.

who.p: Staff of the Minister's office and the department your application is sent to. Your details are not sold or used for any other purpose.

ai.p: The pages are read with the help of an AI service to save time. Staff check every detail against your letter before it is saved.

keep.p: As long as needed to act on your application, and as required by government record-keeping rules.

rights.p: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can ask to see or correct your details, or raise a grievance, using the contact details below.

status.p: It shows only the stage of your application, never your personal details, and needs both your token number and your mobile number.

service.p: It lets you check the status of an application you handed in at the Janata Darbar.

status.p: The status is shown for your information. The department's written reply is its official decision.

use.p: Please look up only your own application. Do not try to guess other token numbers.

availability.p: The service may be unavailable at times for maintenance. Your application is not affected.

samples.title: Try a sample letter
samples.hint: Fictional letters for demos and testing. They are scanned, read and routed like real ones.

welcome.tagline: Your application, heard and followed through
welcome.lead: Bring your letter to the Janata Darbar. Staff photograph it, you get a token number on the spot, and you can follow it until the department resolves it.

status.title: Already handed in an application?
status.hint: Enter the token number from your SMS or slip.

s1.title: Hand over your letter
s1.body: At the Darbar, staff photograph every page. You keep your original.

s2.title: Get a token
s2.body: You get a token number by SMS straight away.

s3.title: Follow it
s3.body: The application goes to the right department. Check its progress here at any time.

stories.title: Citizens' stories
stories.note: Illustrative examples for this demonstration. These are not real citizens.

staff.title: For office staff
staff.body: Scan, check and forward applications, and follow them up.

water.name: Sunita P.
water.quote: For three months our society got water for barely half an hour a day. I got a token at the Darbar and followed it by SMS. The supply was restored in 12 days.

crop.name: Ramesh K.
crop.quote: Unseasonal rain ruined my paddy. The panchanama was done within a week of the Darbar, and I could see every step on the status page.

pension.name: Shantabai M.
pension.quote: My pension had stopped and I did not know whom to ask. My grandson checked the token on his phone. The pension started again the next month.

leopard.name: Vasant J.
leopard.quote: A leopard was seen near our hamlet several nights in a row. After the Darbar, the forest department sent a team and set up a cage within days.
